open_points.subject: answer_request depth validation
open_points.text: After the token check, before any other bound is checked and before the message is parsed, walked or canonicalised, the depth of the request message as received, as canonical_bytes defines depth, MUST be within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant, measured on the message text without recursion, else invalid_request; a deeper request never reaches a recursive walk.
open_points.question: Which passage must change: must canonical_bytes expose or accept a depth limit, or must the prompt define another permitted way to obtain the depth that canonical_bytes defines?

open_points.subject: answer_request response id for excessive-depth bodies
open_points.text: After the token check, before any other bound is checked and before the message is parsed, walked or canonicalised, the depth of the request message as received, as canonical_bytes defines depth, MUST be within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant, measured on the message text without recursion, else invalid_request; a deeper request never reaches a recursive walk.
open_points.other_text: The id of every response is the body's id member when the body is one JSON object whose id is a string or an integer, and null otherwise; reading it checks nothing and decides nothing.
open_points.question: For an over-depth JSON object containing a string or integer id, must the implementation parse or walk enough of the body to return that id, or must the depth-refusal response use null without applying the every-response id rule?
